newsitem.title: USA: U.S Aug consumer credit up $3.3 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.S Aug consumer credit up $3.3 billion.

text.p: U.S. consumer installment credit grew $3.3 billion in August at a 3.5 percent annual rate, after rising a revised $7.3 billion in July at a 7.6 percent annual rate, the Federal Reserve said Monday.
The Fed said it was the slowest pace of monthly consumer credit growth in more than three years, since it contracted by $200 million in May 1993.
Previously, the Fed said July consumer credit outstanding had risen by $7.7 billion but it revised that down.
Wall Street analysts had forecast that August consumer credit would rise much more strongly by $7.3 billion.
Auto credit outstanding barely rose in August by $200 million at a 0.5 percent annual rate, far below July's $2 billion increase, when auto loans were growing at a 6.7 percent annual rate.

Revolving or credit-card debt in August also grew much more slowly, by $2.8 billion at a 7.5 percent annual rate, only half the $5.6 billion July advance, when it was expanding at a 15.2 percent annual rate.

Other credit, which includes consumer bank loans but not real estate mortgages, grew by $400 million at a 1.3 percent annual rate in August after contracting by $300 million at a 1.3 percent rate in July, the Fed said.
Before seasonal adjustment, the total outstanding consumer credit in August was $1.163 trillion, up from $1.154 trillion in July and up from $1.057 trillion in August 1995.
